title: Views and Materialized Views
subtitle: CREATE VIEW, materialized views with REFRESH, CTEs with WITH
author: KERNAL Team

content.code:
-- A view is a stored SELECT query — query it like a table
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW published_posts AS
  SELECT
    p.id,
    p.title,
    p.created_at,
    u.username AS author
  FROM posts p
  JOIN users u ON u.id = p.user_id
  WHERE p.published = TRUE;

-- Use the view like a table
SELECT * FROM published_posts ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 10;
SELECT * FROM published_posts WHERE author = 'alice';

-- Views are virtual — no data stored, query runs every time
-- DROP VIEW IF EXISTS published_posts;

-- Materialized view: stores results on disk
-- Fast to query, but must be refreshed when data changes
CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW monthly_revenue AS
  SELECT
    DATE_TRUNC('month', created_at) AS month,
    COUNT(*) AS orders,
    SUM(total_price) AS revenue
  FROM orders
  WHERE status = 'completed'
  GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('month', created_at)
  ORDER BY month;

-- Create index on the materialized view
CREATE INDEX idx_monthly_rev_month ON monthly_revenue(month);

-- Query it (data is from last refresh)
SELECT * FROM monthly_revenue WHERE month >= '2026-01-01';

-- Refresh the data (blocks reads during refresh)
REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW monthly_revenue;

-- Non-blocking refresh (keeps old data available during refresh)
REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY monthly_revenue;
-- Requires a UNIQUE index on the view

-- CTEs make complex queries readable
WITH
  -- Step 1: get users with their order counts
  user_orders AS (
    SELECT user_id, COUNT(*) AS order_count
    FROM orders
    WHERE status = 'completed'
    GROUP BY user_id
  ),
  -- Step 2: classify users
  classified AS (
    SELECT
      u.id,
      u.email,
      uo.order_count,
      CASE
        WHEN uo.order_count >= 10 THEN 'VIP'
        WHEN uo.order_count >= 3  THEN 'Regular'
        ELSE 'New'
      END AS tier
    FROM users u
    JOIN user_orders uo ON uo.user_id = u.id
  )
SELECT tier, COUNT(*) AS count
FROM classified
GROUP BY tier;

questions.question: What is the key difference between a VIEW and a MATERIALIZED VIEW?
options: Views can be indexed; materialized views cannot
Views run the query every time they are queried; materialized views store the result and must be explicitly refreshed
There is no difference — both store query results
questions.explanation: A VIEW is a virtual table — it re-runs the underlying SELECT query every time you query it. A MATERIALIZED VIEW stores the query result on disk — it is fast to query but shows potentially stale data until you run REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW. Use views for simplicity; use materialized views for expensive aggregation queries that don't need real-time freshness.

faq.q: Should I use a CTE or a subquery?
faq.a: CTEs are better for readability when you reference the result multiple times or when the logic has multiple steps. Subqueries are fine for one-off use. PostgreSQL 12+ inlines CTEs by default (optimizes them as subqueries), so performance is usually the same.

examples: Materialized views are used for daily/hourly aggregations that would be too slow to compute on every page load
Views provide a stable API over tables — application code queries the view, the underlying table structure can be refactored without changing the app
